title: U.S. House · Virginia's 9th District
area: Southwest Virginia, including Abingdon, Christiansburg, Bristol and the coalfield counties along the Kentucky, Tennessee and West Virginia borders.

context.text: This is an open contest on the Democratic side: Joy Powers won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.6% of the vote over Adam Murphy (36.1%) and Douglas Crockett (12.2%). Incumbent H. Morgan Griffith advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after it was canceled. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate the race Solid/Safe Republican as of September 22, 2026.

candidates.name: H. Morgan Griffith
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Morgan Griffith is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to a ninth term representing Virginia's 9th District. A Salem attorney who spent 17 years in the Virginia House of Delegates, including as House Majority Leader, he was first elected to Congress in 2010. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where he chairs the Health Subcommittee.

background.text: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1958; his family moved to Salem, Virginia, when he was an infant, and he graduated from Salem's Andrew Lewis High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Emory & Henry College in 1980, graduating with honors, and a J.D. from the Washington and Lee University School of Law in 1983.
Returned to Southwest Virginia after law school and practiced law for nearly three decades.
Served in the Virginia House of Delegates from 1994 to 2011, representing the 8th District; was elected House Majority Leader in 2000, the first Republican in Virginia history to hold that position.
Won the 9th District seat in November 2010, defeating Democratic Rep. Rick Boucher, who had held it for 28 years.

Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee: chaired its Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee in the 118th Congress, chaired the Environment Subcommittee at the start of the 119th Congress, and is now chairman of the Health Subcommittee.
Also serves on the Committee on House Administration and, per his office's biography, is Vice Chairman of the Committee on Rules, to which Speaker Johnson appointed him in the 119th Congress.

Told Cardinal News that the work he is most proud of in Congress is fighting the fentanyl epidemic, including passage of the bipartisan Drug Quality and Security Act on compounding pharmacies, and that a current priority is the Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act on maternal health.
According to his official biography, he is married to Hilary and they have three children.

record.text: Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, chairing its Subcommittee on Health in the 119th Congress; also a senior member of its Environment and Communications & Technology subcommittees.
Serves on the Committee on House Administration, which oversees House operations, Capitol security and federal-election oversight.
Appointed by Speaker Johnson to the House Committee on Rules in the 119th Congress and serves as its Vice Chairman.
Chaired the Energy and Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations in the 118th Congress.

candidates.name: Joy Powers
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.6% of the vote over Adam Murphy and Douglas Crockett.

summary.text: Joy Powers is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Morgan Griffith. A fourth-generation cattle farmer and small business owner from Bedford County, she ran unsuccessfully for the Virginia House of Delegates in 2025. She describes herself as a Southwest Virginia native running on a "HOME Plan" covering health care, economic opportunity, markets and education for the region.

background.text: Describes herself as raised in 4-H and FFA, and as living and working on her family's 350-acre cattle farm in Bedford, Virginia; Cardinal News calls her a fourth-generation cattle farmer.
Describes herself as a small business owner and a mother to a son she adopted through foster care.

According to her campaign website, she has served as superintendent of the Bedford County Fair, as a member of the Bedford County Agricultural Economic Development Advisory Board, and as founder of Restore the Harvest, an agricultural education organization.

Her campaign website lists involvement with Virginia FFA, Virginia 4-H, Chamblissburg Ruritans, the Virginia Simmental Association and the Virginia Farm Bureau, and says she has been a foster care parent and advocate.
Ran as the Democratic nominee for Virginia House of Delegates District 51 in 2025 and lost to Republican incumbent Eric Zehr, 75.4% to 24.5%.
Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for the 9th District, defeating Adam Murphy and Douglas Crockett.

priorities.text: Universal healthcare paired with direct investment in rural hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, EMS, mental-health and maternal care, and the healthcare workforce.
priorities.quote: I believe healthcare is a human right, and I support universal healthcare. But universal coverage alone will not fix the healthcare crisis in Southwest Virginia if there is nowhere close to home to receive care.

priorities.text: Rebuilding rural economic infrastructure, including rail, roads, broadband, energy, water/sewer systems, industrial sites, agriculture and manufacturing.
priorities.quote: My HOME Plan focuses on rebuilding the foundations of a real rural economy: rail, roads, broadband, energy, water and sewer infrastructure, industrial sites, small businesses, agriculture, manufacturing, and the trades.

priorities.text: Full federal funding for Title I, IDEA special education, Head Start, school nutrition, career and technical education, and investment in rural school buildings and teacher pay.

positions.summary: Says healthcare is a human right and supports universal healthcare, paired with investment in rural health infrastructure.
positions.quote: I believe healthcare is a human right, and I support universal healthcare.

sources.title: Griffith seeks a ninth term in the 9th District. This time, he faces a cattle farmer from Bedford County.

researchNotes: Joy Powers' campaign website (joyforva.com) was loaded for her biography; her priorities and quotes are drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses, which count as her own words.
